datasets.name: ds_aq1_year
datasets.displayName: AQ1: totals and share going to the leading destinations, by year (Query 2)
queryLines:
SELECT
  t.year,
  t.total_travelers,
  t.places_reporting,
  q.leading_destination_share_pct
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      year,
      SUM(total_travelers) AS total_travelers,
      COUNT(*) AS places_reporting
    FROM
      tourism_activity
    WHERE
      year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023
      AND activity_eligible
    GROUP BY
      year
  ) t
    JOIN (
      WITH province_avg AS (
        SELECT
          province_psgc,
          AVG(total_travelers) AS avg_travelers
        FROM
          tourism_activity
        WHERE
          year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023
          AND activity_eligible
        GROUP BY
          province_psgc
      ),
      leading AS (
        SELECT
          province_psgc
        FROM
          province_avg
        QUALIFY
          RANK() OVER (ORDER BY avg_travelers DESC) <= 10
      )
      SELECT
        a.year,
        SUM(
          CASE
            WHEN l.province_psgc IS NOT NULL THEN a.total_travelers
            ELSE 0
          END
        )
          * 100.0
          / SUM(a.total_travelers) AS leading_destination_share_pct
      FROM
        tourism_activity a
          LEFT JOIN leading l
            ON a.province_psgc = l.province_psgc
      WHERE
        a.year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023
        AND a.activity_eligible
      GROUP BY
        a.year
    ) q
      USING (year)

datasets.name: ds_aq1_rank
datasets.displayName: AQ1: top and bottom 10 by overnight travelers
queryLines:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT province_name AS place, region_name, unit_type, year, total_travelers, tourism_rank,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY total_travelers ASC) AS rank_from_bottom,
         CASE WHEN tourism_rank <= 10 THEN 'Top 10' ELSE 'Bottom 10' END AS rank_group
  FROM tourism_activity WHERE year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023 AND activity_eligible)
WHERE tourism_rank <= 10 OR rank_from_bottom <= 10

datasets.name: ds_aq1_map
queryLines:
SELECT province_name AS place, region_name, unit_type, year, latitude, longitude, total_travelers,
       ROUND(tourism_intensity_per_1000, 0) AS tourism_intensity_per_1000, intensity_rank,
       CASE WHEN tourism_intensity_per_1000 < 100 THEN 'Under 100' WHEN tourism_intensity_per_1000 < 300 THEN '100-300'
            WHEN tourism_intensity_per_1000 < 1000 THEN '300-1,000' ELSE '1,000 or more' END AS intensity_band
FROM tourism_activity
WHERE year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023 AND intensity_eligible AND latitude IS NOT NULL

datasets.name: ds_aq1_leading
queryLines:
SELECT q.province_name AS `Province`, e.region_name, e.unit_type, q.avg_travelers_rank AS `Rank (2019-2023 average)`,
       ROUND(q.avg_travelers_2019_2023, 0) AS `Average overnight travelers per year, 2019-2023`
FROM (
SELECT province_psgc,
       province_name,
       AVG(total_travelers)                                    AS avg_travelers_2019_2023,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(total_travelers) DESC)        AS avg_travelers_rank,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(total_travelers) DESC) <= 10  AS is_leading_destination
FROM tourism_activity
WHERE year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023
  AND activity_eligible
GROUP BY province_psgc, province_name
) q JOIN tourism_economy e USING (province_psgc)
WHERE q.is_leading_destination
ORDER BY q.avg_travelers_rank

datasets.name: ds_profile
queryLines:
SELECT place, region_name, unit_type, latitude, longitude, is_leading_destination, destination_group, map_group, group_label, travelers_2023, ROUND(earnings_per_visitor, 0) AS earnings_per_visitor, small_base_2023, ROUND(afs_share_of_gdp_pct, 2) AS afs_share_of_gdp_pct, gdp_per_capita_thousand, wealth_group, is_lagging, is_high_output, what_the_data_shows, what_to_look_at
FROM (
WITH leading AS (
  SELECT province_psgc,
         RANK() OVER (ORDER BY AVG(total_travelers) DESC) <= 10 AS is_leading_destination
  FROM tourism_activity
  WHERE year BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023 AND activity_eligible
  GROUP BY province_psgc
),
base AS (
  SELECT e.province_psgc, e.province_name, e.region_name,
         e.travelers_2023, e.status_2023,
         e.afs_gva_current_2023, e.afs_share_of_gdp_pct, e.gdp_per_capita_current_2023,
         COALESCE(l.is_leading_destination, false) AS is_leading_destination,
         CASE WHEN e.status_2023 <> 'not_reported'
                   AND e.travelers_2023 > 0
                   AND e.afs_gva_current_2023 IS NOT NULL
              THEN e.afs_gva_current_2023 * 1000.0 / e.travelers_2023
         END AS earnings_per_visitor
  FROM tourism_economy e
  LEFT JOIN leading l ON e.province_psgc = l.province_psgc
),
medians AS (
  SELECT median(CASE WHEN earnings_per_visitor IS NOT NULL THEN travelers_2023 END) AS median_travelers,
         median(earnings_per_visitor)                                               AS median_earnings_per_visitor,
         median(gdp_per_capita_current_2023)                                        AS median_gdp_per_capita
  FROM base
),
classified AS (
  SELECT b.*,
         b.gdp_per_capita_current_2023 < m.median_gdp_per_capita AS is_lagging,
         b.travelers_2023 < 10000                                 AS small_base_2023,
         CASE
           WHEN b.earnings_per_visitor IS NULL THEN 'Insufficient data'
           WHEN b.travelers_2023 >= m.median_travelers
                AND b.earnings_per_visitor >= m.median_earnings_per_visitor THEN 'Many visitors, high earnings per visitor'
           WHEN b.travelers_2023 >= m.median_travelers                     THEN 'Many visitors, low earnings per visitor'
           WHEN b.earnings_per_visitor >= m.median_earnings_per_visitor    THEN 'Few visitors, high earnings per visitor'
           ELSE 'Few visitors, low earnings per visitor'
         END AS quadrant
  FROM base b
  CROSS JOIN medians m
),
labelled AS (
  SELECT *,
         CASE quadrant
           WHEN 'Many visitors, high earnings per visitor' THEN 'Established'
           WHEN 'Many visitors, low earnings per visitor'  THEN 'Busy but low-earning'
           WHEN 'Few visitors, high earnings per visitor'  THEN 'Small but high-earning'
           WHEN 'Few visitors, low earnings per visitor'   THEN 'Limited activity'
           ELSE 'Insufficient data'
         END AS group_label,
         CASE
           WHEN quadrant = 'Insufficient data' THEN 'Not enough data to place in a group'
           WHEN quadrant = 'Many visitors, high earnings per visitor' THEN 'Many visitors, and high output per visitor'
           WHEN quadrant = 'Many visitors, low earnings per visitor'  THEN 'Many visitors, but low output per visitor'
           WHEN quadrant = 'Few visitors, high earnings per visitor'  THEN 'Few visitors, but high output per visitor'
           ELSE 'Few visitors, and low output per visitor'
         END AS what_the_data_shows,
         CASE
           WHEN quadrant = 'Insufficient data' THEN NULL
           WHEN is_leading_destination THEN 'Do its visitors also reach nearby provinces?'
           WHEN quadrant = 'Many visitors, high earnings per visitor' THEN 'Do the benefits reach nearby provinces?'
           WHEN quadrant = 'Many visitors, low earnings per visitor'  THEN 'Where does visitor spending go?'
           WHEN quadrant = 'Few visitors, high earnings per visitor'  THEN 'What keeps visitor numbers low?'
           ELSE 'How does tourism compare with other sectors here?'
         END AS what_to_look_at,
         quadrant IN ('Many visitors, high earnings per visitor', 'Few visitors, high earnings per visitor') AS is_high_output
  FROM classified
)
SELECT l.*, e.unit_type, e.latitude, e.longitude,
       l.province_name AS place,
       CASE WHEN l.is_leading_destination THEN 'Leading destinations' ELSE 'Beyond the leading destinations' END AS destination_group,
       CASE WHEN l.is_leading_destination THEN 'Leading destination' ELSE l.group_label END AS map_group,
       CASE WHEN l.is_lagging THEN 'Lagging (below-median GDP per capita)' ELSE 'Not lagging' END AS wealth_group,
       ROUND(l.gdp_per_capita_current_2023 / 1000, 1) AS gdp_per_capita_thousand
FROM labelled l
JOIN tourism_economy e USING (province_psgc)
) p
WHERE TRUE

lines: # What are we missing when we only look at the usual destinations? **Business question:** How can tourism activity and tourism-related output across Philippine provinces be analysed to identify destinations that may warrant greater attention for tourism development?

## Why this matters

Philippine tourism is concentrated in a few places: in 2023, the 10 leading destinations received **43.7% of all overnight travelers**. The DOT's National Tourism Development Plan 2023-2028 responds with Goal 4, equalized tourism development: opening more of the country to tourism and supporting destinations beyond the established ones. ProvInsights gives a consistent province-by-province view of tourism activity and tourism-related output, so the provinces that are easy to miss become visible.

## Before ProvInsights

Tourism data (DOT), economic data (PSA) and place codes (PSGC) come from different sources, in different formats, with place names and boundaries that change over time. Comparing provinces meant collecting, cleaning and aligning them first.

**Our pipeline** ingests the sources, cleans and validates them, and aligns them to **100 reporting units** (Bronze → Silver → Gold → Analytics). This dashboard is where that consistent province-level view shows up.

## How to use this dashboard

| Page | Question it answers |
| --- | --- |
| **1. Where visitors go** | AQ1: Which provinces have the highest and lowest tourism activity, and how is it distributed? |
| **2. Visitors and output per visitor** | AQ2: How do provinces compare on both the number of visitors and the tourism-related output per visitor? |
| **3. Output and income** | AQ3: Is high tourism-related output per visitor found only in higher-income provinces? |
| **4. Provinces to watch** | AQ4: Which provinces beyond the top 10 destinations warrant closer attention, and what does the data show for each? |
| **Definitions** | The terms, how each is calculated, and what the data can and cannot show |
| **Appendix A and B** | Supporting: recovery compared with 2019, overall and by traveler type |

## Try one question

*Which lower-income provinces outside the top 10 already generate high output per visitor?* Open **4. Provinces to watch**, set **Lagging = Yes** and **High output per visitor = Yes**. The map and list narrow to these provinces, each with what the data shows and what to look at next.

# Definitions and data notes

| Term | Definition | How it is computed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Province (reporting unit)** | One of the 100 areas we compare: 82 provinces, 16 highly urbanized cities that DOT reports separately, the City of Isabela, and NCR. Cities that DOT counts inside a province (for example, Lucena in Quezon) stay in that province | PSGC codes, aligned across years |
| **Tourism activity** | Number of overnight travelers in a province in a year | total_travelers |
| **Overnight travelers (visitors)** | Travelers reported by DOT as staying overnight in accommodation establishments. Not unique visitors, and not same-day visitors | DOT |
| **Tourism intensity** | Overnight travelers relative to population (page 1 map) | Overnight travelers ÷ population × 1,000 |
| **Leading tourist destinations** | The 10 provinces with the highest average annual overnight travelers from 2019 to 2023 | Average over the eligible years, ranked; rank ≤ 10 |
| **Tourism-related output** | Gross value added of accommodation and food services (A&F), current prices, from PSA. A proxy, because PSA publishes tourism value added only nationally | A&F GVA, 2023 |
| **Output per visitor** | How much hotel and restaurant output a province generates for each overnight traveler, in pesos | A&F GVA (thousand PHP) × 1,000 ÷ overnight travelers, 2023 |
| **Groups (quadrant)** | Established (many visitors, high output per visitor), Busy but low-earning (many, low), Small but high-earning (few, high), Limited activity (few, low) | Each province compared with the 2023 medians of travelers (279,150) and output per visitor (₱8,652) |
| **High output per visitor** | Output per visitor at or above the 2023 median | ≥ ₱8,652 (the Established and Small but high-earning groups) |
| **GDP per capita** | Provincial GDP per person at current prices, from PSA | 2023 |
| **Lagging (lower-income) provinces** | Provinces whose 2023 GDP per capita is below the median of all provinces with data. An income indicator, not a measure of poverty | Below ₱140,165 in 2023 |
| **Tourism share of the economy** | How much of a province's economy is hotel and restaurant activity (used to order the priority list) | Current-price A&F GVA ÷ current-price GDP × 100, 2023 |
| **Priority provinces** | Provinces beyond the leading destinations with enough data to be placed in a group, lagging first, then by tourism share of the economy | 83 provinces in 2023 |
| **Small base** | Fewer than 10,000 overnight travelers in 2023: output per visitor may look high only because travelers are few | Kept in the list, marked "Check before naming" |
| **What the data shows / What to look at** | What the province's group says, and a question it raises. Not a recommendation | From the group |

**Proxy note:** hotel and restaurant output (A&F) stands in for tourism's economic output, because PSA publishes tourism value added only nationally. A&F does not capture jobs, other tourist spending (transport, tours, souvenirs), or where the income goes. Residents also eat out and stay in hotels, so A&F overstates tourism somewhat.

Missing values stay blank and are never treated as zero. Provinces DOT doesn't report (BARMM provinces and Sulu) have no traveler measures, rank or group. Medians, groups and the lagging flag are relative positions among provinces with 2023 data, not national benchmarks.

**Out of scope:** access, infrastructure, investment, governance, safety and workforce readiness. The data cannot measure them, so the dashboard raises questions rather than recommending interventions.
